picks.line_source: AgentBets reporting FanDuel; Oct 5, 2026, 10:01 UTC (Action Network carried Kansas State -2.5 in the same window)
picks.case: The matchup the number misses: Houston's run defense (65.4 rushing yards allowed per game) meets a Kansas State offense that wants to run it (240.8), and Kansas State on SI documented seven plays of 20+ yards allowed in the Cincinnati loss — the explosive-play vulnerability Houston's defense can force the game away from. Houston arrives 4-1 having won three straight.
picks.race_effect: A Houston road win reshuffles the Big 12 middle and drops Kansas State to 3-2 with the Cincinnati loss already on the sheet.

picks.line_source: AgentBets reporting FanDuel; Oct 5, 2026, 10:01 UTC (Action Network carried Wake Forest -3 in the same window)
picks.case: Third-down arithmetic: NC State converts 53.4% of its third downs against a Wake defense letting opponents convert 42.5% — and the common-opponent check shows essentially no separation (each beat Louisville by three: Wake 30-27, State 31-28). Wake's 84.8 penalty yards per game is the other free yardage source.
picks.race_effect: Both enter 4-1/3-2 in the ACC pecking order behind Miami and SMU; the winner stays on the conference-title undercard.

picks.line_source: AgentBets reporting FanDuel; Oct 5, 2026, 10:01 UTC (Friday game, Oct 9)
picks.case: Iowa's 12.6 points allowed per game against a Washington offense converting just 29.0% of third downs and drawing 77.8 penalty yards a game — the recipe for the low-possession game Iowa wants on a Friday night. The Huskies' +5 turnover margin is the counterweight that keeps this a field-goal number.
picks.race_effect: Washington has already lost to USC at home; a second home loss effectively ends the Big Ten at-large conversation at 3-3.

trap.line: Penn State -1.5 (DraftKings via Blue Chip Analytics, updated Oct 5; VSiN reported DK opened USC -2.5 before the reversal)
trap.why: The trap writes itself: a 5-1 USC team getting points from a Penn State side on consecutive losses (24-20 Wisconsin, 13-34 Northwestern), with the winning-record narrative pulling public money to the underdog. The evidence says lay the wood anyway: Penn State's pass defense allows 119.6 yards per game — aimed directly at USC's 311.7-yards-per-game passing identity — and the Trojans carry a negative turnover margin against the Nittany Lions' +6. VSiN documented DraftKings opening USC -2.5 and REVERSING to Penn State -1.5: the market already did the trap analysis. Take the favorite, not the story.
